about: The documents behind the hazards of the red cabbage pH lab's seven bottles (hazards.json) and behind the safety card of its primer. Every one was read and none is kept. Five are safety data sheets of the default supplier fetched and read for this lab on the retrieval date, with its browser page saved as text; one is a government record fetched that day; seven are sheets that earlier labs' manifests list, written here exactly as they are there so that the build lists each once: those were not fetched again, and were read in the copies those labs saved, each checked against the hash that lab recorded. `fetchedSha256` is the sha256 of the file as it was fetched or saved. Each `supports` row names in `field` what it supports, gives in `prints` what the document prints, and says in `where` where that is. A row whose field ends in `notCarried` is something read and left out, with the reason.

sources.citation: Flinn Scientific, Inc. Safety Data Sheet: Hydrochloric Acid 6 M - 12 M (Concentrated), SDS number sds_395; revision date December 3, 2018 (read on 2026-10-05; no copy is kept).

supports.where: The sheet's title, after the words Hydrochloric Acid: the strengths the sheet is for. The buffer on the bench is about 0.13 M, far below them; a buffer of this kind is made up from the concentrated acid, and the bottle carries the statements of the most dangerous form it is made from (spec 5.2). Not fetched again: read in the copy an earlier lab saved, whose hash is the one that lab recorded.
Under the title, after the words Revision Date, and again at the foot of the sheet: the revision that was read.
Under the title, after the words Signal Word. The sheet prints it in capitals; the record stores Danger.

supports.prints: Causes severe skin and eye burns and damage (H314+H318)
supports.where: Section 2, the first of the three hazard classes it lists: category 1, for corrosion of the skin and damage to the eyes. The record stores the sheet's own line, with its code or codes in front as printed, then a colon and the statement. Precautionary statements, whose codes begin with P, are not hazard statements and are not carried into the record.
Section 2, the second of the three: category 4, for acute toxicity by mouth and by breathing in. The two codes are stored in the order the sheet prints them.
Section 2, the last of the three: category 1, for corrosion of metals. The section prints no other hazard code.

Section 2, the second of the three hazard classes it lists. The first is H314, burns of the skin and damage to the eyes; the third is H303, that it may be harmful if swallowed, which is milder than the H302 on the tile and is not said again.

The heading of section 8. Under it: eye protection, gloves and protective clothing, washing the hands after, and a hood or a room where the air is well changed. Section 4 has the eyes rinsed with water for several minutes and a poison centre or a doctor called at once. Section 10 keeps the acid from strong oxidisers, bases, amines and alkali metals.

Read and not carried. The heading of section 13, under which the sheet says that the rules that may apply are looked at first and that one of the supplier's own numbered methods (#24b) is one option. Why: the note gives no method of disposal (spec 5.2).
